R6C-bear-walk-0004.name: By Chadsey Creek
R6C-bear-walk-0004.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R6C-bear-walk-0004.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2008 (18 years old), 50 m NW: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 16 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Chadsey Creek 100 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: MU 6-12 is not listed in the Region 6 black bear rows (my reading of the table).

plan: Drive: from Village of Daajing Giids, about 38 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.99284, -131.9901, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 420 m E, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 2 m, about 9 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, season: VERIFY. Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 6-12, Region 6. Season: no general open season (synopsis page 50, 95%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R6C-bear-walk-0004.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 6-12: about 67 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.4 km and about 2 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
